  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****
  COVID-19 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING MEETINGS OF
  THE INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL AND OTHER CITY LEGISLATIVE BODIES

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood City Council and other City legislative bodies will be conducted
pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which allows the City to use teleconferencing for
members of the public to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION

  1. Members of the public who wish to attend a public meeting and address the City Council or other
  legislative body during a public meeting must use the call-in option noted below:

  l  Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments telephonically by dialing:
  l Dial-in for Closed Session: 1-669-900-6833 Meeting ID: 825 5030 7638 Passcode: 024788
  l Dial-in for Open Session: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694, using the specific
  access codes detailed below for the respective City Council Dates:

  l May 3, 2022 – Access Code: 2128671#
  l May 10, 2022 – Access Code: 8559062#
  l May 17, 2022 – Access Code: 8737771#
  l May 24, 2022 – Access Code: 4278317#

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on items
appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.
 In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on items
appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS

The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to submit comments and/or to observe a
public meeting. The following alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience only and
the disruption in service to any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body from
taking further action on an agenda item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members of
the public should use the call-in option above.

2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or
subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00
a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact
the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
  details.
  l Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

4. Public attendance at Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) to view
meeting and make public comments via audio/video.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard,
First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and
aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  May 24, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
May 24, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Padilla, Morales, and
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Kailyn Austin  City Clerk Staff Assistant
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk/Acting Successor Agency Secretary/Acting Housing Authority
Secretary/Acting Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum
as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/Joint Powers Authority Members Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Joint Powers Authority Member
  Dotson.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
personnel present were as follows:
  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk/Acting Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Kailyn Austin  City Clerk Staff Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority.

Council Member Padilla left the dais at the hour of 2:04 p.m.
   May 24, 2022

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.
  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated May
  20, 2022, in the amount of $1,833,443.98 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Morales, and Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, and Padilla.

  Council Member Padilla returned to the dais at the hour of 2:05 p.m.

125  RESOLUTION NO. 22-83 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL,
  AND ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES OF THE CITY, TO CONTINUE TO
  CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM MAY 24,
  2022, THROUGH JUNE 23, 2022, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361. Staff
  report dated May 24, 2022, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members adopt a resolution authorizing the City Council, and all other legislative bodies
  of the City, to continue to conduct public meetings via teleconference from May 24,
  2022, through June 23, 2022, pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 22-83 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND
  ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES TO CONTINUE TO CONDUCT
  PUBLIC MEETINGS VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM MAY 24, 2022,
  THROUGH JUNE 23, 2022 PURUSANT TO AB 361.

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on April 26, 2022, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR THE CITY
  PARKING LOTS REHABILITATION PROJECT. Staff report dated May 24, 2022,
  was presented recommending authorization of payment of Invoice No. 195891 submitted
  by All American Asphalt for the City Parking Lots Rehabilitation Project.

  2
   May 24, 2022

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $32,429.10. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

142  FISCAL YEAR 2021 - 2022 MIDYEAR BUDGET REVIEW REPORT RECEIVED
  AND FILED. Staff report dated May 24, 2022, was presented presenting the Fiscal Year
  2021-2022 Midyear Budget Review Report.

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Budget Manager, presented the Midyear Budget Review Report
  for the Fiscal Year 2021-2022.

  Council Member Morales left the dais, at the hour of 2:31 p.m.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais, at the hour of 2:33 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Authorize the City Manager to encumber $500,000 at a time for
  a contract that has already been signed by the Mayor if it falls short of funding in the
  Fiscal Year; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to report to the City Council within two
  weeks to get the contract affirmed. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Mark Weinberg, Assistant City Manager spoke on the General Fund and Capital
  Improvement Projects (CIP).

  Following discussion, Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 22-84 ADOPTED – ADOPTION OF A LIST OF PROJECTS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 FUNDED BY SB 1; INCLUSION OF SAID
  FUNDS IN THE FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 BUDGET AUTHORIZED. Staff report
  dated May 24, 2022, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution adopting a
  list of projects for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 funded by SB 1: The Road to Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 22-84 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE ROAD
  REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  and; 2) Authorize the inclusion of said funds into the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget to be
  appropriated for Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) Local Streets
  Resurfacing projects. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 22-85 ADOPTED – APPROVAL OF THE REVISIONS AND
  EXECUTION OF THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR (“ITC”) JOINT
  POWERS AUTHORITY (“JPA”) AGREEMENT. Staff report dated May 24, 2022,
  was presented recommending adoption of a resolution approving revisions and
  executions of the Inglewood Transit Connector (“ITC”) Joint Powers Authority (“JPA”)
  Agreement.

  3
   May 24, 2022

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Resolution No. 22-85 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING REVISIONS AND
  EXECUTION OF THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR JOINT
  POWERS AUTHORITY AGREEMENT

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 9200000000M550706 APPROVED – LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA);
  MAYOR TO EXECUTE FUNDING AGREEMENT ON BEHALF OF THE CITY
  AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated May 24, 2022, was presented recommending
  approval of Funding Agreement (FA) Number 9200000000M550706 with the Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Authority (LACMTA) and City of Inglewood (Grantee) to
  award funding for the Downtown ITS Project (Project), in the amount of $7,300,000.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 9200000000M550706;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute Funding Agreement Number
  9200000000M550706 on behalf of the City. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

101  ORDINANCE NO. 22-10 ADOPTED – ADDING ARTICLE 5.1 TO CHAPTER 8
  OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (IMC), REGULATING PEDICABS
  AND AMENDING OTHER RELEVANT MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS. Staff
  report dated May 24, 2022, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 22-
  10, adding Article 5.1 to Chapter 8 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), regulating
  pedicabs and amending other relevant Municipal Code Sections.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 22-10 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADDING ARTICLE 5.1 TO CHAPTER 8 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE REGULATING PEDICABS AND
  AMENDING OTHER RELEVANT MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS

  which was introduced at the meeting held May 17, 2022, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  4
   May 24, 2022
